body:
Redline round 4

Reviewed the fix diff from round 3 (da09090..8bad058), and the coverage pass's candidates over the whole pull request at 8bad058.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 8bad058 returned 10 candidates: 7 verified, 2 could not be confirmed, 0 refuted, 1 collapsed into items already reported or settled, 0 already tracked.

Round 3's fixes do what they set out to do. An empty or null disposition now runs on as none, two statements are read in order, overrides and calls are told apart one way, and the override warning names the disposition the person chose. What remains is mostly text that one of those fixes left behind or narrowed. That includes a resume clause chosen by agent type rather than by the stop (R4-4), an intake rule narrower than the reader it cites (R4-2), and the R2-4 'task of its own' ask, which was given to calls but not to overrides (R4-9). The repository has no scheduled or queued work (no routes/console.php), so no overlap applies. The fix diff's doc change is in docs/running.md.

### Other items (7)

- **R4-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `docs/running.md:126` · The doc keeps the first of two statements but does not say a first statement outside the three leaves the call with none
- **R4-2** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:246` · Intake drops only null and '' but its comment and the standard say it reads a disposition as run() reads an error
- **R4-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:247` · Removing the disposition key goes through Object.fromEntries/filter where rest destructuring does it in one line
- **R4-6** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:911` · Two comments still say only an override or a rule call has no statement, and that a call's decision names no disposition
- **R4-7** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3857` · A stray entry beside a call stated fix or accept is dropped only from the workflow's list, so the committed shape.md still shows it as deferred
- **R4-8** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3857` · `stated` is a plain object, so a returned id like 'constructor' reads as a statement
- **R4-9** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3909` · An override is held to a task of its own, but neither the overrides prompt nor the agent file asks for one

### Could not confirm (2)

- **R4-4** · correctness · low · unconfirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:578` · The resolve resume clause is chosen by agent type, so the autopilot 'could not apply' stop also tells the agent to correct what the error names
  Would confirm it: A resumed autopilot resolve after 'autopilot could not apply the shaper's recommendation', showing whether the rerun guesses a task for the unclear recommendation or still leaves it under unresolved.
- **R4-5** · nit · low · unconfirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:901` · RESOLVE_SCHEMA requires `decided` for a resolve whose prompt never asks for it
  Would confirm it: A relaunch, under the new script, that replays an overrides-only resolve result recorded before #99, showing whether the harness accepts it without `decided`.

Each item has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, with what it decided and why.

### Candidates set aside (1)

<details>
<summary>Refuted, collapsed or already tracked</summary>

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:578` · Altitude: the resume wording is chosen by agent type (`opts.agentType === 'redline:redline-resolve'`), not by what caused the stop, so the new replay.md rule ('a step whose stop is the workflow's own check of what that step returned is told so') is a special case for one agent. · duplicate: 3: same cause as candidate 3, reported as R4-4. `resolveFix` is chosen by `opts.agentType` (line 578), not by what stopped the run, and R4-4's proposed fix is the flag on the stop that this candidate suggests. (candidate 3, `workflows/redline-loop.js:578`: unconfirmed R4-4)

</details>

comments.body:
**R4-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**The doc keeps the first of two statements but does not say a first statement outside the three leaves the call with none**

Since R3-3's fix (90ec7e4), `resolveWith` picks the first statement per id before it reads the value (workflows/redline-loop.js 3811-3812). So `decided: [{id:'R1-1', disposition:'mitigate'}, {id:'R1-1', disposition:'fix'}]` gives two messages: the warning `the resolve agent stated a disposition for R1-1 more than once; the first is kept` (3814) and the stop `the resolve agent stated no disposition for R1-1` (3819). The loop case `misstatedFirst` (tests/loop-test.mjs, added in round 3) pins that pair. docs/running.md line 126 says only 'A second statement for one call is dropped too: ... the first is kept' and lists 'a call with no statement at all' as a stop. It never says that a statement outside fix, defer and accept counts as none, or that this holds when it is the first of two. A reader of the doc expects the valid second statement to be dropped and the run to go on, and instead sees the warning beside the stop. The R3-3 fix changed the code and the test but not this bullet. Round 3's plan named docs/running.md, for R3-4's sentence.

Proposed fix: Update docs/running.md, section "Deferred items", bullet "A deferral you chose at a call": after 'the first is kept', add that a statement outside fix, defer and accept is no statement, so a first one like that stops the round at `resolve` even when a valid second one follows it.

**R4-2** · nit · low · confirmed

**Intake drops only null and '' but its comment and the standard say it reads a disposition as run() reads an error**

R3-1's fix (54d6218) drops a decision's `disposition` only when it is `null` or `''` (line 246). The comment above it (241-244) says 'as run() reads an agent's error (#42)', and the new sentence in agent-os/standards/workflow/agents.md says 'a decision's disposition at intake is read the same way'. `errorText` (594-597) also trims the text and reads the strings '""', "''" and 'null', and whitespace, as empty. Intake does neither, so `disposition: 'null'`, `'""'` or `' '` still reaches the `else if` at 248 and fails the launch with `args.decisions must give a disposition of fix | defer | accept`. This is the refusal R3-1 removed for '' and null. The conditions it needs: a session writing one of those strings, which no documented path does. The skill records a disposition only as fix, defer or accept. The comment also says 'where the check above refused it', but the check it means is the `else if` below, in the same loop.

Proposed fix: Either read the field through the same rule as errorText (trim a string, and treat '', '""', "''", 'null' and null as none), for example with a small shared helper, or narrow the comment and the agents.md sentence to 'an empty string or null'. Also reword 'the check above' to say the check refused it before #108, R3-1.

**R4-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**Removing the disposition key goes through Object.fromEntries/filter where rest destructuring does it in one line**

R3-1's fix (54d6218) builds a copy of the decision without `disposition` like this: `Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(entry).filter(([key]) => key !== 'disposition'))` (line 247). `const { disposition: _dropped, ...rest } = entry; decisions[id] = rest` makes the same shallow copy of the entry's own keys without that one. The repository's checks run no linter (.claude/redline/checks.json), so an unused binding draws nothing. The only cost is readability.

Proposed fix: Replace line 247 with rest destructuring, for example `const { disposition: _dropped, ...rest } = entry` and `decisions[id] = rest`.

**R4-4** · correctness · low · unconfirmed

**The resolve resume clause is chosen by agent type, so the autopilot 'could not apply' stop also tells the agent to correct what the error names**

R3-4's fix (a2ba199) adds `resolveFix` to the resume line of every resolve. The test is `opts.agentType === 'redline:redline-resolve'` (578-580), and nothing checks which stop the run is resuming from. One resolve stop is the autopilot `autopilot could not apply the shaper's recommendation for R1-2` (3793-3796). That stop is thrown from what the earlier attempt returned (`out.unresolved`), so the clause's condition ('When that error is the check the workflow runs on what the earlier attempt returned') reads literally onto it. Its instruction, 'correct what the error names, and return the whole result again', then asks the agent to apply the recommendation it had judged too unclear. The agent file's first rule says the opposite: 'Apply, never reinterpret ... do not guess: leave that entry pending'. The same sentence is in agents/redline-resolve.md line 32. A resolve stop from a crash or a guard refusal also gets the clause, though its condition does not match there. The other agents still get only 'the person has since fixed the cause by hand' for a stop that is the workflow's check of their own output, so each new stop of this kind needs another branch keyed by agent (candidate 8). What is traced: the clause is appended to that resume (578-583, 600-605), and the stop takes the resolve label through `lastLabel`. What is not measured: whether an agent reading both sentences guesses a task or leaves the call pending.

Proposed fix: Choose the clause by the stop, not by the agent. For example, set a flag (say `ownCheck: true`) in the `stageError` calls that check the resolve's returned statements, entries and tasks (3819, 3865, 3880, 3896, 3900, 3904, 3911, 3915), carry it into the resume entry, and append the clause only when `resumeLine` reads it. Leave the autopilot 'could not apply' stop without the clause. A loop case resuming that stop, asserting the prompt has no `resolveFix` sentence, pins it.

Could not confirm. Would confirm it: A resumed autopilot resolve after 'autopilot could not apply the shaper's recommendation', showing whether the rerun guesses a task for the unclear recommendation or still leaves it under unresolved.

**R4-5** · nit · low · unconfirmed

**RESOLVE_SCHEMA requires `decided` for a resolve whose prompt never asks for it**

`RESOLVE_SCHEMA.required` includes `decided` for every resolve (line 901). The whole ask for it is in the calls block only (2094-2097), on purpose, so that an overrides-only prompt stays byte-identical to the prompt before #99 (decision 13). Picture a new script running with an agent file loaded before #99. On an overrides-only resolve, neither the prompt nor that agent file mentions `decided`, but the schema still requires it. With the current agent file, step 3 says an override has no entry. Whatever such an agent returns is read only by `firstPerId` for the repeat warning (3811-3815), because `asked` holds calls only. A stray override statement can therefore add a 'stated a disposition ... more than once' warning and nothing else. The other path is the replay the schema comment relies on (913-914), 'A result recorded before #99 holds no list, and can replay only for a resolve with no call'. If the harness checks a replayed result against the current schema, that cached result fails before `out.decided || []` (3811) is reached. The pull request's Known gaps measure only the opposite case, an extra key a schema does not list. Whether the harness checks a cached result against the schema is harness behaviour the repository cannot show.

Proposed fix: Either measure the replay of a cached result with no `decided` under the new schema and record the outcome beside decision 13, or make `decided` optional in RESOLVE_SCHEMA, since `resolveWith` already reads an absent list as empty and every call it reads is checked through `unstated` (3816-3820).

Could not confirm. Would confirm it: A relaunch, under the new script, that replays an overrides-only resolve result recorded before #99, showing whether the harness accepts it without `decided`.

**R4-6** · nit · low · confirmed

**Two comments still say only an override or a rule call has no statement, and that a call's decision names no disposition**

Since R1-2 (a8a1c9d), a call whose decision carries its own `disposition` is asked for no statement: `asked` leaves it out (3816), and the prompt's `anyNamed` sentence (2097) says it has no entry. Two comments from the pull request's first slice (0f406f78) were not updated. (1) The RESOLVE_SCHEMA comment (909-914) says 'one entry per call the resolve applied', names only an override and a rule call as having no entry, and says 'an empty one means no call was applied'. An empty list is also correct when every call applied was named or under a rule. (2) The comment in `isDeferral` (3958-3962) says 'A call's decision names none'. The `decision.disposition` branch just below it (3963-3965) also decides a named call. The repository's standard is that a comment restating a rule changes along with the rule.

Proposed fix: In the RESOLVE_SCHEMA comment, say that an override, a call whose decision names its own disposition and a call left to the person under a rule have no entry, and that an empty list means no call needed a statement. In the isDeferral comment, write 'A call's decision that names no disposition is read from what the resolve agent stated for it'.

**R4-7** · nit · low · confirmed

**A stray entry beside a call stated fix or accept is dropped only from the workflow's list, so the committed shape.md still shows it as deferred**

`strayCall` (3857-3861) removes the entry from `once.kept` before `deferred` takes it, and the warning says 'the entry is dropped, since the statement decides'. The resolve agent's instructions pair the two writes: for a deferral, add the finding under `## Deferred` in shape.md with its draft, 'and return it in `deferred`' (agents/redline-resolve.md step 3, line 23). A stray entry is therefore likely in shape.md as well. Nothing in the workflow edits shape.md (the only rewrite instruction is the shaper's resume clause, line 572). No later prompt tells an agent to remove the entry. The round's spec folder is committed with the round. The record then says R1-1 is deferred with a drafted issue, while its thread reply says 'Applied in <sha>' and no issue was opened. Before this pull request, a filled stray entry beside a call was filed, so shape.md and the outcome agreed. The pull request extends to every answered call, on every dial, the gap an override has had since #103, R2-8 (3831-3851), which is code this pull request did not add. The plan approver reads shape.md and gets only `shaped.deferred` in its prompt (2133-2134). Whether it bounces on the mismatch is agent behaviour, not measured.

Proposed fix: When an entry is dropped as stray, ask the next agent that writes the folder to remove it (for example, a line in the implementer's prompt naming each dropped id: 'remove <id> from ## Deferred in shape.md; it was dropped because the statement decides'). Or say in docs/running.md that the round's shape.md can still list a dropped entry, and that the run's warning and the reply are the record.

**R4-8** · nit · low · confirmed

**`stated` is a plain object, so a returned id like 'constructor' reads as a statement**

`stated` is `{}` (3763). It is read with truthy lookups (`Boolean(stated[item.id])`, 3857), with `===` (3893, 3966), with `in` (4128) and with `Object.keys` (4130). For a deferred entry whose id is an inherited name such as `constructor` or `toString`, `stated[id]` is a function. That id is truthy and not 'defer', so the entry is dropped as a stray, with the warning `... stated its decision as function Object() { [native code] } ...`. The `in` test at 4128 would treat a finding with that id as stated. The conditions: an id outside the workflow's `R<n>-<k>` form, which only an agent's own `deferred` list could carry. No finding id has that form, so in practice the risk is limited to an odd warning for a malformed entry.

Proposed fix: Declare `const stated = Object.create(null)`, or use a Map with `.has()` and `.get()`, so only ids the resolve stated count.

**R4-9** · nit · low · confirmed

**An override is held to a task of its own, but neither the overrides prompt nor the agent file asks for one**

R2-4 was fixed, but still reproduces here for overrides. Its fix (a461d1e) put 'a task of its own, its finding set to the call's id' in the calls block's ask (2097) and in the agent file's `decided` paragraph (line 24). `namedUnplanned` and `namedPlanned` (3909-3916) read an override's files through the same `taskFilesOf(out.tasks, id)` (479), which keeps only tasks whose single `finding` (RESOLVE_SCHEMA 906) equals the id. The overrides block of the prompt (2103: 'fix: plan the full fix as a task, files by path ...') and the agent file's override paragraph (line 21) never say that. docs/running.md line 126 leaves 'of its own' out of the named-decision sentence too ('a fix with no task that names files'). Example: the person overrules decline R1-2 to fix, and the resolve agent folds the fix into R1-1's task (`finding: 'R1-1'`). The round stops at resolve with 'the resolve agent planned no task with files for R1-2, which a disposition override names as a fix', a rule its prompt never gave. An accept override on R1-1 whose task also carries another finding's change stops through `namedPlanned` the same way. Separately, an overrides-only prompt is byte-identical to the one before #99. A result cached under an older script can therefore replay into these stops on a relaunch that runs a newer script, which the pull request's Known gaps say happens on a repository that is not the plugin's own after an update.

Proposed fix: Add the same clause to the overrides block's fix wording, for example 'fix: plan the full fix as a task of its own, its finding set to the override's id, files by path and the test that proves it'. Add it to the override paragraph of agents/redline-resolve.md as well, and add 'of its own' to the named-decision sentence of docs/running.md 'A deferral you chose at a call'. Because this changes the overrides-only prompt, check the replay note in the comment at 2094-2096 and decision 13.
